title: It Snowed 95 Feet in One Winter on This Mountain

scenes.text: One mountain got 95 feet of snow in a single winter.
scenes.keywords: huge snowfall mountain ski lift buried

scenes.text: It's Mount Baker in Washington, in the winter of 1998 to 1999.
That's 1,140 inches, the most snow ever officially recorded in one season.
Stack it up and it's taller than a nine-story building.
Storms roll in from the Pacific, hit the mountain, and dump snow for months.
95 feet of snow. In one winter.

description:
Mount Baker in Washington received 1,140 inches of snow in the 1998 to 1999 season, a world record verified by NOAA.
That is about 95 feet, taller than a nine-story building.
Would you ski here or run?
thumbnail_text: 95 FEET OF SNOW IN ONE WINTER
first_comment: Bonus: the next biggest season on record was 1,063 inches, also at Mount Baker. How much snow is too much for you?
